name: Methane
kicker: CH₄, the simplest hydrocarbon · The main ingredient of natural gas
briefing: Methane is the simplest hydrocarbon: one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms. It is the main ingredient of the natural gas that heats homes and fuels stoves, and it bubbles up from swamps, which is why it was once called “marsh gas.” Cows burp it out as microbes in their stomachs digest grass, and on Saturn’s moon Titan it falls as rain and fills lakes.
answerHtml: Methane (accept CH4 or marsh gas; prompt on natural gas; do not accept “ethane” or “methanol”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: In 1776, Alessandro Volta collected bubbles of this gas by stirring the mud along the shores of Lake Maggiore [“mah-JOR-ay”], and he showed that it could burn. Coal miners feared pockets of this gas, which they called “firedamp,” because it could explode underground.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this gas, the simplest hydrocarbon and the main ingredient in natural gas.

tossups.p: Humphry Davy’s 1815 safety lamp surrounded its flame with fine wire gauze so that the flame could not ignite this gas, which often caused explosions in coal mines. With plenty of air, this gas burns with a hot blue flame in laboratory Bunsen burners.
tossups.r: Cows burp it out as they digest grass. For 10 points, name this gas made of one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms.

tossups.p: In 1944, Gerard Kuiper [“KY-per”] detected this gas in the atmosphere of a moon, the first evidence that any moon has an atmosphere. Sunlight breaks this gas apart high in that moon’s air, and the pieces join into an orange haze of particles called tholins [“THOH-linz”].
tossups.r: That moon, Titan, has lakes of liquid ethane and this compound. For 10 points, name this simplest hydrocarbon.

tossups.p: On the seafloor and in permafrost, molecules of this gas are trapped inside cages of frozen water, forming a substance nicknamed “fire ice” because a lump of it can burn. Thawing permafrost can also release this gas as microbes break down ancient plant remains.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this greenhouse gas, the main component of the natural gas used for heating homes.

tossups.p: In steam reforming, this compound reacts with steam over a nickel catalyst to make most of the hydrogen used in the Haber process. Burning one mole of this compound releases about 890 kilojoules of heat and makes carbon dioxide and water.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this gas, the main ingredient of the natural gas burned in stoves and furnaces.

tossups.p: In ultraviolet light, chlorine atoms can replace this compound’s hydrogen atoms one at a time, eventually producing chloroform and then carbon tetrachloride. Its molecule is a perfect tetrahedron, with bond angles of about 109.5 degrees.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this simplest alkane, a gas with one carbon atom that makes up most of natural gas.

tossups.p: In a famous experiment in the 1950s, Stanley Miller and Harold Urey [“YOOR-ee”] sent electric sparks through a flask of water vapor, hydrogen, ammonia, and this gas, producing several amino acids. Archaea [“ar-KEE-uh”] that live without oxygen make this gas as a waste product.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this simplest hydrocarbon, the main ingredient in the natural gas burned in kitchen stoves.

tossups.p: This gas absorbs red light, which helps give Uranus and Neptune their blue colors. Water, ammonia, and this compound make up much of the hot, slushy “ices” deep inside those two planets, which are called ice giants.
tossups.r: On Earth, it is the main ingredient of natural gas. For 10 points, name this simplest hydrocarbon.

tossups.p: Microbes living in the rumen [“ROO-men”], the first stomach chamber of cattle, sheep, and goats, produce this gas as they help break down grass, a process called enteric fermentation. Scientists have tested adding certain seaweeds to cattle feed to cut down on this gas.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this greenhouse gas that cows burp out, the main ingredient of natural gas.

tossups.p: Because this gas has no smell of its own, gas companies add sulfur compounds called thiols, or mercaptans [“mer-CAP-tanz”], so that people can notice leaks. This gas is lighter than air, so it rises when it escapes.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this main ingredient of the natural gas piped into homes, the simplest hydrocarbon.

tossups.p: Linus Pauling explained the shape of this molecule by mixing one s orbital and three p orbitals on its central atom into four sp³ hybrid orbitals. Those orbitals point to the corners of a tetrahedron, giving bond angles of about 109.5 degrees.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this compound of one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms, the main part of natural gas.

tossups.p: Wetlands are the largest natural source of this gas, and rice paddies, landfills, and termites also give it off as microbes break down plant matter and garbage without oxygen. The amount of this gas in Earth’s air has more than doubled since the Industrial Revolution began.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this greenhouse gas, the main ingredient of natural gas, which cows burp out.

tossups.p: Cooled to about minus 162 degrees Celsius, this compound turns into a liquid, so special tanker ships can carry it across oceans. Its tiny molecules attract one another so weakly that it is a gas at room temperature, unlike larger hydrocarbons such as octane.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this simplest alkane, the main component of the natural gas used to heat many homes.

tossups.p: NASA’s Curiosity rover has measured changing amounts of this gas in the air of Mars’s Gale Crater, which interests scientists because living things on Earth make much of it. On Earth, this gas also forms underground as heat and pressure act on the buried remains of ancient organisms.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this gas, the simplest hydrocarbon, which makes up most of the natural gas burned in stoves.

tossups.p: This gas lasts only about a decade in the air before it breaks down, mostly by reacting with hydroxyl radicals, while carbon dioxide lingers for centuries. Leaks from wells, pipelines, and coal mines release large amounts of this gas.
tossups.r: Ton for ton, this greenhouse gas traps far more heat than carbon dioxide. For 10 points, name this simplest hydrocarbon.

trap.title: Not natural gas or methanol
trap.body: Natural gas is a mixture that is mostly methane, so “natural gas” earns only a prompt. Methane also has close cousins with similar names: ethane (two carbons), propane (three carbons, the fuel in many grills), and methanol (an alcohol with an –OH group, also called wood alcohol). Naming one of those loses the tossup.
trap.fix: “Simplest hydrocarbon,” “one carbon and four hydrogens,” cows, Titan, firedamp, and Volta all mean methane, so say methane instead of natural gas. Two carbons mean ethane, grill tanks mean propane, and an –OH group means methanol.
trap.line: Real answer line: Methane (accept CH4 or marsh gas; prompt on natural gas; do not accept “ethane” or “methanol”)
